items.title: Smart home devices should work without the internet
items.content:
AI;DR: I wrote the first draft, AI helped me edit and rewrite it, and I made the final pass. The rules, setups, and talks are my own.

TLDR; Nothing core in my house depends on a vendor’s server. If the internet goes down, the house keeps running. That’s been rule one for about ten years, and my other rules came out of it. This post has the rules, then both talks I’ve given on home automation, slide by slide.

My Nest integration worked until Google broke the API. That’s the failure I plan around now. The talks have a few more: a Samsung fridge showing a TLS certificate error on its own screen, and a Camp Chef grill controller that needs Wi-Fi to show you the temperature.

Everything that matters runs on hardware I own. That’s Tasmota on ESP boards, an MQTT broker, and Node-RED on a Raspberry Pi. I do use some cloud services, mostly Alexa and a few AWS ones. Alexa is just another way to flip a switch. If it’s down, the wall switches and the wall dashboard still work.

From the first talk, restated in the second:

No internet, no problem. Core stuff has to work with the internet unplugged. Alexa can be a way in, but never the only way.

Don’t remove the old way while adding the new one. If someone tapes a wall switch on so a smart bulb keeps power, I skipped this rule.

Be agile. Rooms get used differently and people move in and out, so it all has to be cheap to change.

Check your automations. I once had four scheduled triggers hitting the same garden pump.

Exceptions must be exceptional. I can break a rule, but only for a reason I’d still agree with six months later.

Added after year five, once more people lived in the house:

A cloud device needs an API with logs or it doesn’t get installed. I don’t want a black box in the house.

Config lives in one place instead of five vendor apps.

More than one way in: an app, Alexa, a QR code, or an NFC tag.

If I keep doing the same steps, they become a routine.

Devices talk pub/sub over MQTT instead of point to point.

No batteries unless they last a year or more between changes. Nobody wants to swap a door sensor battery at 2am.

The build I get asked about most is the Tasmota sprinkler controller . It’s in both talks, and so is the garage door setup, which has been running about as long.

Nobody needs any of this. I like building things that just work in the background, and each automation is a small puzzle.

Everything talks to a cloud now: phones, laptops, thermostats, locks. Those clouds may or may not be up when you need them, so know what you’re signing up for before you plug something in.

Most people start here: a thermostat, a plug, a lock. Each has its own app and account.

Every device lands somewhere on this triangle. A cloud camera is cheap and easy, and it costs you privacy. A switch I flash myself takes longer to set up, but I can hook it into anything. I figure out where a device lands before I buy it.

Someone (often me) automates a light, then has to tape the wall switch on so the smart bulb keeps power. If a switch in a room ever did nothing, this is why.

The better fix is an in-wall Wi-Fi switch. The switch still works like a normal switch and I can still automate it. It’s more work to install than a smart plug, but nobody has to change their habits.

Rule one: if the internet goes down, my lights still turn on.

It’s never done. Rooms get used differently, people move in and out, new devices show up. Whatever you build has to be cheap to change.

The garage cooling flow starts from a manual trigger and checks if the door is closed. Then it opens the door, waits, and turns on the fan. If cooling is already running, it just sends a notification. Small flow, but it has kept the garage from baking more than once.

The door sensor and reed switch both report into a transform step that sets a global garage-closed flag and logs to Grafana. Below that is the chart from a few real days: 21 opens, with spikes showing when each one happened. It’s easy to skip…

items.title: .name grandfathered
items.summary: networking
items.content:
After a long and expensive battle, news just dropped that Verisign is retracting its plan to terminate 22,000 domain names and email redirects. Although they will be closing new registrations for 3rd-level .name domains, all existing domains (including this website) and email redirects will remain indefinitely.

This was a team effort. It was inspiring how many talented people joined this fight. From Doytchin who kicked everything off, to Jim who flew to Bali to make the case to ICANN in person, to Patrik, Troy, Huyen, Keith, Judy, Erik, and Ryan who wrote formal reconsideration requests, to my lawyers Jan, Flip and Diégo who threw the book at ICANN, to Beverly, Stefan, Vaughan, Irv, Pablo, Larry, Lionel, Daniel, Ori, Markus, Kirk, Ed, Jeremy, Stephan, Matija, Jan, Simon, Mark, and Evan who filed letters of support. I'd also like to sincerely thank selected individuals within ICANN who had the courage to stand up against the bureaucracy. Without exception, everyone I spoke with was a remarkable person.

items.title: US air traffic control enters the 21st century, starts to abandon floppy disks
items.content:
US air traffic control enters the 21st century, starts to abandon floppy disks

The FAA will need to come up with more money to finish the wider overhaul, though

Turn your home into a giant crane game with this open source robot

These smart glasses promise to turn your silent mouth movements into text

iFixit dismantles Apple's Duo: 'You'd better baby that screen'

YouTuber built 30-frame-per-second grayscale Game Boy, then open sourced it for all e-paper displays

OpenAI claims 100-plus secret files followed ex-employee back to Apple

The Federal Aviation Administration still uses computers that require floppy disks. But those are finally on the way out within the next few years.

Yes, it’s still 2026, and yes, you read that right: The FAA – the agency responsible for overseeing aviation safety in the US – is finally getting rid of four systems dating back to the 1980s that remain in use at more than 400 facilities around the country, the agency announced  on Thursday.

“Good news America: floppy disks are out, 21st century tech is in,” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in the FAA’s announcement. Only a few decades late, Sean, but we’re sure the flying public appreciates it.

The new system, known as Enterprise Information Display System ( E-IDS ), is designed to consolidate data from various systems into a common digital platform, allowing air traffic controllers to access operational information and alerts needed to manage flights.

E-IDS is replacing four legacy systems: Information Display System 4, used to track weather and operational info; the Automated Surface Observing System Controller Equipment Information Display System, which also relays weather information; the NAS Information Display System, which relays information about airports and other airspace conditions; and the En Route Information Display System (ERIDS), which handles information about flights.

The FAA said E-IDS will improve how Pilot Reports and Notices to Airmen (NOTAMs) are collected and distributed. The agency has had its share of air traffic control SNAFUs, including one in 2023 that temporarily halted domestic flight departures nationwide after someone accidentally deleted a file from the NOTAM system.

The FAA said it has already lined up five facilities to receive E-IDS upgrades: airports in Atlantic City, Nashville, and Rochester, New York, along with data processing hubs in Atlanta and Salt Lake City. The agency plans to install the system at 435 sites by the end of 2028.

That 2028 deadline echoes the ambitious three-year timetable Duffy laid out last year for overhauling the nation's air traffic control system.

Aside from the four systems E-IDS will replace, the FAA has a lot of outdated technology, with the Government Accountability Office saying in 2024 that 51 of the agency’s 138 ATC systems were unsustainable due to lack of parts and funding to sustain or replace them.

Trump’s Big Beautiful Bill allocated $12.5 billion for the FAA’s overhaul efforts, but that’s far short of what’s actually needed. In December of last year, the FAA said that it needed an additional $20 billion to handle upgrade costs, and that appears to still be the case.

"To continue modernizing our air traffic control facility, Secretary Duffy and FAA Administrator Bedford are calling on Congress to pass the Modern Skies Act," an FAA spokesperson told The Register  in an email. That bill is asking for $30 billion to get ATC modernization across the finish line, the spokesperson added.

" It will modernize our air traffic control system, replace crumbling aviation infrastructure, and build world-class airports across the country," they said. In other words, the FAA wants  to get rid of floppy disks, but it's probably not accurate to say they're "out," as Duffy put it.

items.title: Blender 5.3 has been released today 🎉 🥳
items.content:
New features overview by Jonathan Lampel and Wayne Dixon from CGCookie .

Welcome native 3D Gaussian Splats support to Blender 5.3!

Import them as point clouds, experiment with Geometry Nodes, preview them in Workbench, and render them natively with EEVEE or Cycles.

3D Gaussian Splats are commonly used to reconstruct 3D scenes from photos or videos. They consist of many small, soft, transparent blobs that combine to represent complex geometry and shading.

Blender can now import Gaussian Splats from PLY , SPZ , and glTF files, store them as point clouds, process them with Geometry Nodes, and render them in EEVEE, Cycles, and Workbench (solid mode).

PLY file imported as gaussian splats, featuring DOGWALK by Blender Studio.

Gaussian splats are represented as point clouds, using a new type to tell them apart and with special attributes:

scale : A vector represneting the size of the splat.

rotation : A quaternion to control the rotation of the splat.

radiance:base : 4D Vector as base (DC) radiance of the splats, followed by opacity.

radiance:sh_{index} : Coefficients of the spherical harmonics bands >= 1. The order is <L=1 M=-1> , <L=1 M=0> , <L=1 M=1> , <L=2 M=-2> … where L is the band index and M is the basis function.

By default, a 3D Gaussian Splat is rendered using an emissive shader. The radiance attribute provides access to the resolved radiance of the splat at the current shading point.

There is rudimentary support for making the splat relightable by replacing the Emission node with a hard surface BSDF such as Diffuse BSDF.

Performance is still being optimized. Rendering may produce inaccuracies due to differences between the sRGB space used by most Gaussian Splat authoring tools and Blender’s linear color space, particularly in areas with low opacity and high radiance.

Improved color management interoperability

The Principled BSDF now supports Dispersion !

Turn ordinary glass and diamonds into beautiful little rainbows by splitting white light into its colorful components.

Cycles Dispersion overview on YouTube by Chris Tyler

Butterflies specter shader by Cartesian Caramel

With Dispersion in the Transmission panel, the Principled BSDF can now reproduce the characteristic rainbow effect seen in glass and gemstones. This corresponds to OpenPBR v1.1.1.

Roughness anisotropy is also now supported by the Glass BSDF and the transmission component of the Principled BSDF. It behaves just like anisotropy for specular reflections.

Blender 5.3 integrates DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction as a new denoiser, delivering cleaner images faster by upscaling and reusing samples from previous frames.

Think Cycles looks with EEVEE responsiveness.

NVIDIA DLSS brings near-final render quality to the viewport, making lighting and look development faster and more responsive while virtually eliminating flickering between frames during animation playback.

Find it in the Denoise panel under Render properties, Sampling.

DLSS denoising requires NVIDIA driver version 620 or newer.

Blender 5.3 brings native support for NVIDIA RTX Spark devices running Windows 11, including memory optimizations.

Material Lighting nodes allow authoring how the Material reacts to Lights.

This can, for example, be used for toon and stylized shading, but also for complex physical effects like iridescence.

All the nodes you need to adjust lighting to your liking.

Per-light data, evaluation, and shadow information are now available in the Shader Editor, giving you more control over how materials respond to individual scene lights.

Four new nodes and two that received a “Light” mode/space:

Light Accumulation : Evaluates its inputs for each light in the scene and accumulates the results.

Light Info : Exposes light data properties (Color, Power, and Position).

Light Evaluation : Evaluates position-dependent light properties (Diffuse/Specular Term, Attenuation Mask, Direction, and Distance).

Shadow Raycast : Outputs a shadow mask value for the light…
items.title_ko: Blender 5.3 출시… 3D 가우시안 스플랫 네이티브 지원 추가
items.summary_ko: Blender 5.3이 출시됐다. 이번 버전부터 3D 가우시안 스플랫을 기본 지원해 PLY, SPZ, glTF 파일을 포인트 클라우드로 가져올 수 있고, 지오메트리 노드로 가공하거나 EEVEE, Cycles에서 직접 렌더링할 수 있다. 3D 가우시안 스플랫은 사진이나 영상으로 만든 3D 장면을 표현하는 데 흔히 쓰이는 방식이다.
items.content_ko: Blender 5.3의 주요 기능을 소개하는 글이다. 이제 PLY, SPZ, glTF 파일에서 3D 가우시안 스플랫을 가져와 포인트 클라우드로 저장할 수 있으며, 지오메트리 노드로 처리하고 EEVEE, Cycles, Workbench(솔리드 모드)에서 렌더링할 수 있다. 가우시안 스플랫은 작고 부드러운 반투명 입자들이 모여 복잡한 형상과 음영을 나타내는 방식이다. 입자에는 scale(크기), rotation(회전을 제어하는 쿼터니언), radiance:base(기본 방사 값과 불투명도를 담은 4차원 벡터), radiance:sh_{index}(1차 이상 대역의 구면 조화 계수) 같은 속성이 붙는다. 예시로 Blender Studio의 DOGWALK를 PLY 파일로 가져온 장면이 소개된다. 기능 개요는 CG Cookie의 Jonathan Lampel과 Wayne Dixon이 작성했다.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.title: The hardest tarball
items.summary: unix
items.content:
Here is a curiosity: an archive that can be constructed using a single GNU tar invocation, that is extracted in 8 distinct ways depending on what tool you use.

It creates an archive hardest.tar from three files file ./file empty in sequence, where file is repeated so that GNU tar stores the second one as a hard link, and empty is empty. Exploiting the unique path of the second entry, the hard link is renamed to café . This triggers tar to create a pax header to store the file name as UTF-8. We add a size=512 record to the pax header, which overrides the default size=0 from the hard link. The value 512 is not a coincidence: it is exactly the size of a tar header.

Visually, this archive has the following structure, with two basic interpretations based on whether a hard link can have a size or not.

Now, POSIX says that data blocks for a hard link “may be included” in pax archives, but the implications of this are not entirely clear. So the 512 bytes after the hard link are its data, and not the header of empty as we archived it? How can a hard link have different contents from its previous counterpart file ?

This archive gives by far the richest and most surprising results I've encountered so far when extracting it with well-known tar utilities and libraries. The results below were produced using the latest releases of all packages at the time of writing.

This group is reasonable in principle: they ignore the size on the hard link, and extract file , its hard link café , and empty .

This is the system tar utility of macOS, which is closer to POSIX in spirit regarding the concept of size on hard links, and writes the 512 bytes into the hard link. The end result is that file now contains the tar header of empty .

This group agrees with bsdtar that the 512 bytes are data of the hard link, but doesn't write them into the hard link. Instead, they skip forward over the data, and you are left with just file and café , without empty .

This is where you begin to need more imagination. Because café contains data, a separate file is created that contains the header of empty as data, while file keeps its original contents.

Makes café a separate, empty file, and also extracts empty . Why not?

Does not extract café at all, but to make up for it, it creates an empty directory PaxHeaders next to file and empty .

R has an entirely different approach: it extracts empty with 512 null bytes. It mistakenly applies the size to empty instead of the hard link, and those 512 bytes are from an end-of-archive marker.

Haskell's tar would be exactly like GNU tar, if only it did not have string decoding issues, which turn the file café into cafÃ© on disk (in the year 2026, this is not a rendering quirk of your browser).

These implementations reject the tarball. I believe this is the best thing you can do, even if it's technically not POSIX-compliant.

This tarball is one of 134 tricky tarballs that I'm collecting and categorizing in my test suite haampie/tar-minefield , developed since the last post. Its website https://stoppels.ch/tar features a big table that shows how implementations deal with all these cases, as well as detailed info per test case. A variant from the tarball of this post is included as a test case .

If you'd like to discuss this, send me an email at firstname[at]lastname.ch .

items.title: Incident Report: unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing | AISI Work
items.content:
You can access the full technical report here.

AISI’s role is to evaluate and understand the capabilities of frontier AI models, surfacing potential risks before they reach the public. To assess what these models can do, including whether they could be misused for cyberattacks, we test them under deliberately permissive conditions: with access to the open internet, and with some safety filters disabled.

On 28 th July 2026, AISI's Security Team detected unusual data transfers leaving our research systems during a routine cyber evaluation. On investigation, we found that some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations. We declared a security incident and, within roughly one hour of discovery, had contained it and begun a full investigation.

The incident stemmed from a single evaluation where agents were given a task of solving a cyber security challenge. We ran this challenge 122 times across several models. Our investigation found that in 10 of those runs, an AI agent took autonomous, unsanctioned action on the live internet, targeting real people and organisations. In total, we catalogued 19 such actions. Almost all of this behaviour (17 actions) came from a single model, Anthropic's Mythos 5, with 2 actions involving OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol with cyber classifiers (mechanisms to prevent misuse) disabled. In the most serious case, an agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project. In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering  — creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code. A human maintainer caught and refused to approve the malicious code.

These attempts were unsuccessful, and our investigations have not evidenced any resulting real-world harm. But this is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world.

Importantly, this was not a case of a model escaping its secure test environment, or ‘sandbox’. As was standard in our cyber testing, we had intentionally permitted internet access, and model-provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled - conditions that do not reflect how frontier models are made available to the public. We do this to best assess the maximum capability of models. These configuration choices have been common practice in frontier AI evaluations. The specific models in question, in the configurations in which we tested them are not commercially available and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios.

Ahead of publishing this blog, we notified GitHub (the developer platform accessed during the evaluation) of the agents' malicious activity, which included actions that GitHub has confirmed violated their terms of service. We worked together with GitHub to remove artefacts left behind by the agent, and to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with. We have also contacted other affected parties. We also intend to work with METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) to conduct an independent third-party review – we are still working through the scope of this review with them.

This incident should be interpreted with caution and nuance. To some degree, our evaluation design choices and specific configurations enabled the behaviour. Nonetheless, the activity undertaken by the agent show signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviours, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate.

There are important caveats to bear in mind: we observed a small number of events under very specific conditions, and cannot yet say how likely such behaviour is in different contexts or outside of testing environments. items.title: Anthropic targets valuation of up to $1.4tn in stock market flotation
items.content:
Trading in Anthropic shares is expected to begin next week. Photograph: Dado Ruvić/Reuters

Trading in Anthropic shares is expected to begin next week. Photograph: Dado Ruvić/Reuters

Anthropic targets valuation of up to $1.4tn in stock market flotation

Claude chatbot developer had been reported to be aiming for $2tn IPO on Wall Street before investors cooled on AI

Anthropic is seeking a valuation of up to $1.4tn (£1.1tn) in its imminent stock market flotation , short of the $2tn that had been expected before investors started to question the durability of the AI boom.

The developer of the Claude chatbot was widely reported to be targeting a $2tn initial public offering on Wall Street but its sights have been set lower, according to a US regulatory filing on Tuesday.

Anthropic is aiming to raise up to $64.4bn by selling 825m shares in the IPO priced up to $78 a share. The California-based company will also raise a further $26bn via a separate private placement deal ⁠with cornerstone investors including the Google parent, Alphabet, and the chipmaker Nvidia.

An extra $9.7bn could be raised from a so-called greenshoe offering, which kicks in if investor demand is high and would take the total amount raised by Anthropic to approximately $100bn if the shares sold at the top end of the price range.

I read Anthropic's 92-page risk factor document, so you don't have to – video explainer

At the upper bracket of the $70-$78 per share price range, Anthropic would be worth $1.4tn on a fully diluted basis – which means taking into account all the common shares in the company in existence, including employee stock options.

Trading in Anthropic shares is expected to begin next week.

Investor jitters over the AI boom were crystallised last week when the US midterm elections produced victories for datacentre opponents. This has added to already existing concerns, such as how quickly – or if at all – companies can generate a return on their spending on AI infrastructure.

Brian Hopkins, a principal analyst at Forrester Research, said the midterm elections gave investors the chance to correct valuations that they were beginning to have concerns about, because of worries about the financial sustainability of the AI build-out. The election results brought those concerns to a head, Hopkins said.

“The market needed an excuse to correct itself a little bit in terms of valuations,” he said. “The US election spook is what has caused it.”

As a consequence, Anthropic’s valuation has also been lowered from an anticipated $2tn, he added.

The largest ever stock market listing is Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which joined the US stock market with a valuation of $1.78tn, raising $75bn. The company, whose assets include Musk’s rocket launch business and the X social media platform, is now worth just under $2tn.

However, the $100bn that could be raised in the Anthropic offering will exceed the amount raised by SpaceX.

Dario Amodei, Anthropic’s chief executive, is selling about $260m worth of shares in the float, as are his six fellow co-founders. At the top of the price range the co-founders’ stakes will be worth more than $18bn each.

A Chinese spying scandal enveloping Nvidia , a cornerstone company for AI investors, also threatens to overshadow the industry but has not affected share prices so far – other than Nvidia’s.

The updated Anthropic filing stated that the company’s annual revenue is now running at $81bn as of 31 October, up $10bn from the previous month.

Anthropic’s main expenditure is on the computing power, from datacentres, that is key to developing and operating its AI systems. According to its prospectus, Anthropic has compute purchase commitments and lease agreements of more than $70bn over the next 12 months and more than $450bn by 2030, with a further $450bn due by 2045.

In a podcast appearance earlier this year, Anthropic’s Amodei explained how compute commitments had to be matched by revenue growth.

items.title: AI usage generates a fragile codebase
items.content:
I can only speculate as to the reasons why I was laid off from Meta in May, but I suspect that one of the reasons is that I was a little bit more resistant to adopting AI/LLMs as coding tools than some of my peers. Don't get me wrong, I generated at least 90% of my code using AI in my last few months there, which was the minimum for a decent rating. But AI didn't 10X the amount of code I was writing. It didn't even 2X it.

I was focused on code quality. I saw the code being pushed by some of my peers who were heavily reliant on AI, and I saw that it was brittle code. There were many subtle issues that would lead to tech debt in the long term, and even some glaring issues were ignored by very good programmers. For instance, I saw one of the best programmers on my team try to merge code that used javascript events for mouseover CSS effects rather than using the :hover selector, which is a totally unscalable way of writing mouseovers.

Now I'm employed at another large tech company and I've fully made the switch to generating 100% of my code using AI because that's the expectation today. Still, I can see lots of people becoming aware that this isn't a sustainable way to continue development of a large scale SaaS product. AI tends to solve the problems that can fit within its context window very well, but it's totally oblivious to the long term issues that can't be understood in that relatively small frame.

In this post I'm going to list four ways that AI usage results in a fragile codebase that isn't resilient to the demands of highly available and highly scalable SaaS applications.

By the way, every word of this article was written by a human. Even though the following image was generated by AI, this article isn't AI slop.

Here are the four most common ways that I have seen AI generating a fragile codebase.

One of the most obvious failures of modern LLMs is that they tend to write simplistic automated test cases that don't cover the things that matter to humans. Frequently I see AI agents writing lots of tests of get/set methods which are trivial and don't typically require much testing. When AI writes e2e tests, they tend to only cover the cases which are already covered in the codebase. In other words, the AI writes tests only covering one type of user, or only covering surface level interactions. This creates massive gaps in the test coverage that are invisible to developers because they aren't captured by the line level coverage metric.

AI also tends to write overly complex code. It frequently uses two or three helper methods when a single one would suffice. It tries to follow coding guidelines, such as DRY, to a fault, without realizing that the added complexity of that rigidity makes the code more difficult for human developers to debug or understand.

And that's the third issue with AI codebases: Humans don't understand them. The longer a company relies on AI agents to generate the code, the fewer developers are going to understand the codebase. This means that developers can't do the things that are necessary to build a resilient codebase. They don't understand the data structures and algorithms well enough to see when a pull request contains a new abstraction that doesn't work with the pre-existing structures.

AI moves too quickly for human developers to maintain a high quality bar. Each pull request comes faster than the prior one and has to be reviewed in even less time. This leads to developers skimming the code and missing crucial details that result in long term tech debt. Small quality issues like testing gaps and poorly named variables accrue in the codebase until it becomes a morass of spaghetti code.

If you're unsure whether coding agents are harming your codebase or not, then you might look for the following symptoms of a fragile, AI-generated codebase.

items.title: Alleged Chinese Spy Alice Huang Flaunted Deep Personal Bond With NVIDIA’s Jensen Huang, Who Celebrated Her Every Birthday Every Year And Created $7.5 Billion AI GPU Network
items.content:
The relationship between NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang and Alice Huang wasn’t a short-term fling that spiraled into something deeper before the controversy disseminated around the globe. According to the latest report, shortly after Huang admitted to the affair and NVIDIA fired up an independent board investigation , new details have come to light, stating that Alice not only used her personal intimacy with the Chief Executive as a primary marketing tool to build a $7.5 billion hardware conduit directly into China-linked data pipelines, but she also boasted about her romance publicly.

Freshly baked bits published by The Information state that Alice Huang had zero technical experience in the semiconductor sector, but she abruptly entered the AI hardware market in 2023 and rapidly accumulated unprecedented industry clout across Asia by boasting about her close, personal relationship with Jensen Huang. Sources familiar with the matter revealed that she regularly posted pictures of herself alongside the CEO on her private WeChat feed and bragged to prospective clients that Huang celebrated her birthday every year by treating her to dinner or sending expensive gifts.

The romance yielded incredible rewards. Where established global clients need to wait months or years for NVIDIA’s high-end AI accelerator shipments, Alice Huang was rapidly accepted as a key player in the GPU giant’s regional footprint. Despite remaining intentionally vague about her job description, she quickly made regular appearances at NVIDIA’s annual partner events in China, solidifying her standing as a member of Jensen’s inner circle.

The affair materialized a GPU shipment network that other companies could only dream of, with Alice Huang’s husband, Kang Wei, and her sister also involved in these operations. At the heart of it all, we have Shanghai Century Litong, which was incorporated in June 2023. Just four months after its inception, the aforementioned firm became one of NVIDIA’s most coveted customers, securing critical priority access to restricted AI accelerators.

Another entity that comes into the equation was Megaspeed, a Singapore-registered data center business where Alice served as a top executive. Megaspeed alone imported an astonishing $4.6 billion in NVIDIA hardware between 2023 and 2025, operating facilities throughout Southeast Asia under the pretext of servicing regional cloud clients like Alibaba. However, federal investigators grew convinced that large hardware shipments were being diverted across customs barriers to Shanghai Century Litong.

Sadly, NVIDIA successfully intervened  before the authorities could find a connection, with the investigation moving from the U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security to the Department of Justice. Alice’s husband, Kang Wei, was a private equity investor who first got acquainted with Jensen in the 2010s and, just a decade later, this relationship blossomed into a $7.5 billion business in restricted AI computing power.

As Jensen Huang’s upcoming November 18 congressional briefing  approaches, we learn more about the depths of his infidelity, and just a week from now, we might have a truckload of juicy details prepared for you, so stay tuned for more updates.

items.title: Day 8 - The infamous "grep" and other text processors
items.content:
Day 8 - The infamous “grep” and other text processors

Complementary video: Text Processing and other useful command line tools

Your server is now running two services: the sshd (Secure Shell Daemon) service that you use to login; and the Apache2 web server. Both of these services are generating logs as you and others access your server - and these are text files which we can analyse using some simple tools.

Plain text files are a key part of “the Unix way” and there are many small “tools” to allow you to easily edit, sort, search and otherwise manipulate them. Today we’ll use grep , cat , more , less , cut , awk and tail to slice and dice your logs.

The grep command is famous for being extremely powerful and handy, but also because its “nerdy” name is typical of Unix/Linux conventions.

Dump out the complete contents of a file with cat like this: cat /var/log/apache2/access.log

Use less to open the same file, like this: less /var/log/apache2/access.log - and move up and down through the file with your arrow keys, then use “q” to quit.

Again using less , look at a file, but practice confidently moving around using gg , GG and / , n and N (to go to the top of the file, bottom of the file, to search for something and to hop to the next “hit” or back to the previous one)

View recent logins and sudo usage by viewing /var/log/auth.log with less

Look at just the tail end of the file with tail /var/log/apache2/access.log (yes, there’s also a head command!)

Follow a log in real-time with: tail -f /var/log/apache2/access.log (while accessing your server’s web page in a browser)

You can take the output of one command and “pipe” it in as the input to another by using the | (pipe) symbol

So, dump out a file with cat , but pipe that output to grep with a search term - like this: cat /var/log/auth.log | grep "authenticating"

Simplify this to: grep "authenticating" /var/log/auth.log

Piping allows you to narrow your search, e.g. grep "authenticating" /var/log/auth.log | grep "root"

Use the cut command to select out most interesting portions of each line by specifying “-d” (delimiter) and “-f” (field) - like: grep "authenticating" /var/log/auth.log| grep "root"| cut -f 10- -d" " (field 10 onwards, where the delimiter between field is the ” ” character). This approach can be very useful in extracting useful information from log data.

Use the -v option to invert the selection and find attempts to login with other users: grep "authenticating" /var/log/auth.log| grep -v "root"| cut -f 10- -d" "

The output of any command can be “redirected” to a file with the “>” operator. The command: ls -ltr > listing.txt wouldn’t list the directory contents to your screen, but instead redirect into the file “listing.txt” (creating that file if it didn’t exist, or overwriting the contents if it did).

If you didn’t find the file /var/log/auth.log you’re probably using a minimal version of Ubuntu (it can be your own local VM or a version in one of the VPS). That minimal image is, well… minimal. It only has the systemd journal available and it didn’t come with the old syslog system by default.

But don’t worry! To get that back, sudo apt install rsyslog and the file will be created. Just give it a few minutes to populate before working on the lesson.

It also be missing a few of the other programs we use in the challenge, but you can always install them.

Re-run the command to list all the IP’s that have unsuccessfully tried to login to your server as root - but this time, use the the “>” operator to redirect it to the file: ~/attackers.txt . You might like to share and compare with others doing the course how heavily you’re “under attack”!

See if you can extend your filtering of auth.log to select just the IP addresses, then pipe this to sort , and then further to uniq to get a list of all those IP addresses that have been “auditing” your server security for you.

Investigate the awk and sed commands. When you’re having difficulty figuring out how…

items.title: Blender 5.3 released with Gaussian Splat support
items.content:
New features overview by Jonathan Lampel and Wayne Dixon from CGCookie .

Welcome native 3D Gaussian Splats support to Blender 5.3!

Import them as point clouds, experiment with Geometry Nodes, preview them in Workbench, and render them natively with EEVEE or Cycles.

3D Gaussian Splats are commonly used to reconstruct 3D scenes from photos or videos. They consist of many small, soft, transparent blobs that combine to represent complex geometry and shading.

Blender can now import Gaussian Splats from PLY , SPZ , and glTF files, store them as point clouds, process them with Geometry Nodes, and render them in EEVEE, Cycles, and Workbench (solid mode).

PLY file imported as gaussian splats, featuring DOGWALK by Blender Studio.

Gaussian splats are represented as point clouds, using a new type to tell them apart and with special attributes:

scale : A vector represneting the size of the splat.

rotation : A quaternion to control the rotation of the splat.

radiance:base : 4D Vector as base (DC) radiance of the splats, followed by opacity.

radiance:sh_{index} : Coefficients of the spherical harmonics bands >= 1. The order is <L=1 M=-1> , <L=1 M=0> , <L=1 M=1> , <L=2 M=-2> … where L is the band index and M is the basis function.

By default, a 3D Gaussian Splat is rendered using an emissive shader. The radiance attribute provides access to the resolved radiance of the splat at the current shading point.

There is rudimentary support for making the splat relightable by replacing the Emission node with a hard surface BSDF such as Diffuse BSDF.

Performance is still being optimized. Rendering may produce inaccuracies due to differences between the sRGB space used by most Gaussian Splat authoring tools and Blender’s linear color space, particularly in areas with low opacity and high radiance.

Improved color management interoperability

The Principled BSDF now supports Dispersion !

Turn ordinary glass and diamonds into beautiful little rainbows by splitting white light into its colorful components.

Cycles Dispersion overview on YouTube by Chris Tyler

Butterflies specter shader by Cartesian Caramel

With Dispersion in the Transmission panel, the Principled BSDF can now reproduce the characteristic rainbow effect seen in glass and gemstones. This corresponds to OpenPBR v1.1.1.

Roughness anisotropy is also now supported by the Glass BSDF and the transmission component of the Principled BSDF. It behaves just like anisotropy for specular reflections.

Blender 5.3 integrates DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction as a new denoiser, delivering cleaner images faster by upscaling and reusing samples from previous frames.

Think Cycles looks with EEVEE responsiveness.

NVIDIA DLSS brings near-final render quality to the viewport, making lighting and look development faster and more responsive while virtually eliminating flickering between frames during animation playback.

Find it in the Denoise panel under Render properties, Sampling.

DLSS denoising requires NVIDIA driver version 620 or newer.

Blender 5.3 brings native support for NVIDIA RTX Spark devices running Windows 11, including memory optimizations.

Material Lighting nodes allow authoring how the Material reacts to Lights.

This can, for example, be used for toon and stylized shading, but also for complex physical effects like iridescence.

All the nodes you need to adjust lighting to your liking.

Per-light data, evaluation, and shadow information are now available in the Shader Editor, giving you more control over how materials respond to individual scene lights.

Four new nodes and two that received a “Light” mode/space:

Light Accumulation : Evaluates its inputs for each light in the scene and accumulates the results.

Light Info : Exposes light data properties (Color, Power, and Position).

Light Evaluation : Evaluates position-dependent light properties (Diffuse/Specular Term, Attenuation Mask, Direction, and Distance).

items.content:
9. november 2026 Links to blog articles look better when they’re accompanied by an image.

If the HTML head has a meta tag like this, it will happen automatically:

content = "https://eaj.no/posts/graph-images-with-typst/og.png"

My previous, tedious workflow for these kinds of images was to go to unspash.com ,

search for something like structure or archive , and then select an image

I thought would fit the theme of the post. Being both boring and error-prone,

I abandonded that process and set up a pipeline that generates image cards at build-time instead.

Typst is a tool that generates high-quality documents from a simple markup language.

it works great for math whilst also keeping the day-to-day text formatting syntax bearable.

As a small taste, this snippet (adapted from the Typst README )

#set page ( width : 10cm , height : auto , margin : 1cm )

The Fibonacci sequence is defined through the

recurrence relation $ F _ n = F _ ( n-1 ) + F _ ( n-2 ) $ ,

with $ F _ 1 = #fib_1 $ and $ F _ 2 = #fib_2 $ .

It can also be expressed in _closed form:_

F _ n = round ( 1 / sqrt ( 5 ) phi . alt ^ n ) , quad

By default the typst CLI will create a PDF, but it can also make PNGs. The above image was created with the command

But if you’d rather create something with a bit more pizzazz, by all means. How about

#set page ( width : 1200pt , height : 630pt , margin : 80pt , fill : rgb ( "#FF1493" ))

#set text ( font : "Comic Sans MS" , fill : white , lang : "no" )

text ( size : 72pt , weight : 800 , "Typst very nice" )

text ( size : 24pt , "Would typst again" ) ,

If all of my posts were titled “Typst very nice”, we’d be done, but, alas.

Luckily, typst accepts inputs to a document with --input key=value ,

which is put in a sys.inputs dictionary for the template to read.

#set page ( width : 1200pt , height : 630pt , margin : 80pt , fill : rgb ( "#FF1493" ))

#set text ( font : "Comic Sans MS" , fill : white , lang : "no" )

#let title = sys . inputs . at ( "title" , default : "You forgot the title :(" )

size : if title . len () > 70 { 60pt } else { 72pt } ,

text ( size : 24pt , "Would typst again" ) ,

--input title="Look ma, from the CLI!" fancy-typst-with-input.typ

Let’s move on to generating the images at build-time.

This site is built with Astro, a static site generator .

Articles are written in Markdown, which is then bundled into a

by Astro. The details are irrelevant, what matters is that this lets me

define metadata which I can query through a Javascript API.

The source code for the page template is at src/pages/posts/[id].astro .

There are a few notable things about this file path:

That it is in the src/pages/ directory tells Astro that this should be rendered as a page.

The remainder of the path, /posts/[id] , tells Astro where to put the page.

[id] being in brackets means id is a dynamic parameter which must be defined at build time.

In other words, Astro needs to know every ID when building the site—it can’t generate infinitely many

IDs. A function called getStaticPaths exported from the template defines the set:

import { getCollection } from "astro:content" ;

export async function getStaticPaths () : Promise < GetStaticPathsResult > {

const posts = await getCollection ( "posts" ) ;

That is, fetch every article, and use its id as the id parameter.

This is the object returned for the current page:

params : { id : "open-graph-images-with-typst" } ,

/* Everything the template needs to render a post */

By default Astro will generate an HTML file, but it can also return other

kinds of responses. Together with this blog post I also put

items.title: Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs
items.content:
Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs

Carmaker points finger at an 'unknown' flaw as customer fallout continues

Nissan has joined the growing list of Oracle customers cleaning up after a cyberattack, warning employees that payroll records, bank details, Social Security numbers, and other personal data may have been stolen.

In a filing submitted to the California Attorney General on Friday, Nissan Americas said Oracle had informed it of "a cyber event" involving the personnel records of "hundreds of companies." The automaker said it later learned Nissan had been "specifically targeted" in the attack.

A notification sent to current and former employees, seen by The Register , says the company believes attackers accessed a haul of sensitive info, including contact and banking information; Social Security, Social Insurance, or other national identification numbers; financial and tax records; and dependent and beneficiary details.

Current and former employees in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Brazil may have been affected, although Nissan said it is still working to determine exactly whose information was exposed.

Nissan said it kicked off its incident response plan after learning of the intrusion, brought in outside security specialists, and has been working with Oracle while keeping law enforcement informed. It plans to offer affected individuals credit or dark web monitoring where available.

The company has also put a few extra locks on the payroll office. Employees can now access pay slips or update direct deposit details only from a corporate network or through a secure VPN, while Nissan adds extra identity checks before processing payroll requests.

The accompanying employee FAQ pins the incident on "an unknown vulnerability in Oracle's PeopleSoft software" and says the campaign is affecting "hundreds of companies and institutions." The document offers no clue as to what the vulnerability is, whether Oracle has patched it, or whether the compromised PeopleSoft environment was hosted by Oracle or by Nissan itself.

The disclosure lands just weeks after researchers linked the ShinyHunters extortion crew to a wave of attacks exploiting a PeopleSoft zero-day . More than 100 organizations and roughly 300 PeopleSoft instances were reportedly compromised before Oracle issued mitigation measures, with the gang claiming to have made off with HR, payroll, and other enterprise data.

Weak security means attackers could disable all of a city's public EV chargers

US regulator tells GM to hit the brakes on customer tracking

21K Nissan customers' data stolen in Red Hat raid

Porsche panic in Russia as pricey status symbols forget how to car

Oracle has said little publicly about the reported attacks and didn't respond to The Register's questions, even as organizations have continued to disclose being caught in the fallout.

Nissan has not confirmed that the incidents are connected, though its California filing lists the breach period as May 27 through June 9, broadly aligning with the previously reported timeline.

The carmaker didn't respond to questions about how many current and former employees are affected, when Oracle first notified it of the breach, and whether the compromise was limited to Oracle-managed systems. ®

items.title: Reddit is turning user conversations into AI-powered product reviews
items.content:
Navigating today’s shopping landscape can be overwhelming. Product information and recommendations are everywhere, and it can be hard to really understand how a product fits into real life. Across Reddit’s communities, people discuss everything from hobbies and daily life to products they’re researching. By offering perspectives grounded in real experience, these conversations provide valuable context in every purchase decision journey. This is why Reddit is the top platform people turn to for trusted perspectives on products, and half of U.S. shoppers say they come to Reddit to validate AI recommendations.

Today, we are starting to test Reddit Reviews ,  a new experience that organizes product conversations from across Reddit into dedicated reviews and highlights the most important takeaways from across our communities. With Reddit Reviews, people can now more easily understand what a product is really like and feel confident deciding whether it’s right for them.

Users can now search for a product's review on Reddit

Lived experience shows up across Reddit communities: in r/skincareaddiction , people share what they’ve tried for dry skin, and in r/espresso , baristas and home brewers compare their setups. These exchanges show how a product can work for different people and what tradeoffs they consider. Reddit Reviews uses AI to both organize these conversations where people describe their product experiences, and to surface the nuance, context, and connection to the original conversation. This next evolution builds on the testing we have done over the past few months; we are excited to continue enhancing product discovery and shopping on Reddit.

People can find a review   by searching for a product or category in the search bar in the Reddit app, or by selecting a highlighted product name in a comment. Then, they can select the review when one appears in the results.

For this initial launch, we're beginning to test with a set of frequently discussed products and categories. If a review isn’t available for a specific product yet, Reddit’s AI Search will provide a response tailored to the question, informed by Reddit conversations.

A review provides a central place to explore what people on Reddit are saying about a product

A review organizes relevant conversations about a product into an easy to digest format with a "what people are saying"   summary. A visual breakdown shows how many of those conversations are positive, mixed, or negative, and themes highlight what people commonly like and dislike to help shoppers understand the tradeoffs. For an espresso machine , themes might include how easy it is for beginners to use or how much counter space it takes up.

Many reviews also include images, prices, and purchase links where supplied by brand and retailer catalogs.

Explore firsthand experiences and compare options

To go deeper, people can browse all comments about a product, using topic filters derived from Reddit conversations to focus on their questions. Clicking on a comment lets them read the original discussion, ask a follow-up question, or join the community for more advice. For people considering alternatives, the review also highlights products people commonly compare.

A review helps people go deep into other options or specific product features

From a review, people can navigate to the full category to discover other similar products discussed on Reddit. Products are grouped around needs that come up in those conversations (such as budget picks or most loved), with filters to help narrow the options.

Categories help people find options they haven'y yet considered

Reddit Reviews will be rolling out over the next few weeks to US users on iOS, Android, and web. The initial selection includes about ~10k products frequently discussed on Reddit across Electronics , Health & Beauty , Home & Garden , and Fashion & Apparel . items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-123084 📢 Source: redhat 💣 CVSS Score: 6.5 (MEDIUM) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True An **expression language injection** has been found in the HeaderContentGuard.permit function in publication.py of the content guard in the **Pulpcore** package. The guard is supposed to check a value in a request header. It saves a jq filter and runs that filter against the header when a client asks for content. The filter is not limited to the header, and jq's env builtin also returns the environment of the content process. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can create a header content guard and attach it to a distribution can save a filter that reads that environment. The content request is allowed or denied according to the filter result. items.title: Announcing .NET 11
items.summary: dotnet, release
items.content:
Today, we’re excited to announce the release of .NET 11! This year’s release makes building modern applications faster, more productive, and has improvements across C# 15, ASP.NET Core, .NET MAUI, and Windows development. With hundreds of runtime optimizations, more responsive SDK tooling, and less overhead in everyday commands, you can spend less time waiting and more time creating. Build richer web and cross-platform applications, take advantage of new C# language features, and explore AI-powered development with improved tools and agentic capabilities.

.NET 11 is a Standard Term Support (STS) release with two years of support under the .NET support policy . STS and Long Term Support (LTS) releases have the same quality and servicing policies; the difference is the length of support. .NET 10 remains a supported LTS option. Stay current with servicing updates whichever release you choose.

Explore .NET 11 with the product teams and community at .NET Conf 2026 . The conference includes product team sessions on November 10 and 11, followed by two days of community sessions.

Watch the Day 1 livestream, including the keynote , or browse the conference session playlist .

Some of the changes we’re most excited for you to try:

C# 15 union types and closed hierarchies help you express the possible states of your application and handle them with compiler-checked patterns.

A Native AOT CLI host and a warm MSBuild server reduce overhead in everyday developer workflows.

ASP.NET Core brings asynchronous validation, OpenAPI 3.2, and new capabilities for Blazor and SignalR applications. Experimental Blazor AI components integrate with the Agent User Interaction Protocol (AG-UI) for advanced agentic web experiences.

Build AI-powered, agentic applications with Microsoft.Extensions.AI (MEAI) for model access, MCP for tool integration, and Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) for agents and workflows.

Put agentic development tools to work with .NET Skills for .NET-specific guidance, .NET MAUI DevFlow for inspecting and testing running apps, and the .NET Upgrade canvas for reviewing modernization progress.

.NET MAUI adopts CoreCLR as its default runtime and improves XAML iteration and native controls.

The libraries add built-in Zstandard compression, simpler process execution, richer JSON support, and new ways to work with in-memory data without copying it first.

The what’s new in .NET 11 overview links to the full details. Here are the changes behind those headlines and how to start using them.

C# 15 is the default language version for projects targeting .NET 11. Union types are one of its biggest additions: a value can be one of a declared set of case types, with conversions from those types and exhaustiveness checking in switch expressions.

Consider a product lookup that either finds a product or reports that it wasn’t found:

ProductLookup result = new Product(42, "Mechanical keyboard");

Product product => $"Found {product.Name}",

ProductNotFound missing => $"No product with ID {missing.Id}",

public sealed record Product(int Id, string Name);

public sealed record ProductNotFound(int Id);

public union ProductLookup(Product, ProductNotFound);

The result type tells a caller which outcomes it needs to handle. There’s no need to use object or an unrelated base class just to put those outcomes behind one return type.

C# 15 also adds closed hierarchies . A closed class limits direct derivation to its declaring assembly, giving the compiler the information it needs to check patterns over the hierarchy. Unions are useful when you want to combine existing types; closed hierarchies fit models where you own the inheritance relationship.

Smaller language features help with everyday code, too. Collection expression arguments let you pass constructor or factory arguments without giving up collection expression syntax:

[with(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase), "Alice", "ALICE", "Bob"];

This prints 2 : the comparer controls equality, so…

items.title: Chinese Hackers Abused Google Workspace Rules to Steal Research and Defense Emails
items.content:
A China-linked espionage group hid inside North American medical, academic, and military research networks for more than a year, quietly stealing sensitive research and defense email.

The way in was a backdoor on their REDCap research servers that stole login credentials. The exfiltration was the unusual part: the attackers rewired the victims' own Google Workspace rules to copy any message matching their keywords to an inbox they controlled.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) laid out the campaign in a report published this week and attributes it with high confidence to a cluster it tracks as UNC6508.

The actor and its REDCap backdoor are not new names; Google first surfaced both in February , in a wider report on state-backed attacks against the defense sector. It did not name the victims, describing them only as multiple organizations across the US and Canada: clinical providers, academic centers, military health institutions, advocacy groups, and health regulators.

Google says it notified them and disrupted the group's infrastructure.

The entry point was REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture), a web platform that hospitals and universities use to build and manage study databases. UNC6508 compromised externally facing REDCap servers.

Google has not pinned down the initial access vector, named a specific CVE, or listed the affected versions, though it saw the group probing older, vulnerable ones.

Around three months after getting in, the group deployed custom malware GTIG calls INFINITERED , which trojanizes REDCap's own system files and does three things.

The earliest known compromise dates to September 2023, with activity continuing through November 2025. Once on the server, UNC6508 ran internal reconnaissance and credential discovery, pulling database and service account credentials, then used those logins to move into the internal network and on to a domain administrator account.

Google does not spell out the exact path to that admin account. With admin rights, the group set up the exfiltration.

The exfiltration rode a feature that was already there. UNC6508 abused content compliance rules, a legitimate Google Workspace admin feature that scans mail for keywords and can copy or forward matching messages.

Similar features exist in other cloud mail suites. The group created a rule, misspelled "Patroit," that watched for nearly 150 keywords, search terms, and email addresses. When a message matched, Workspace silently BCC'd it to an attacker-controlled Gmail address, which Google has since disabled. No malware on the mail server, no separate exfiltration tool, no unusual network traffic. Just a built-in mail feature, turned to copy the organization's secrets to an inbox the attackers owned.

MITRE already catalogs email-forwarding-rule abuse as a known technique. What GTIG flags as new here is the use of domain content compliance rules to do it, a method it says it had not seen from a China-linked actor before.

The rule's keywords mapped to UNC6508's collection priorities: geo-strategic policy, military strategy and equipment, advanced technology including AI and uncrewed vehicles, offensive cyber programs, and medical research. One term stood out for its specificity, chikungunya , the mosquito-borne virus behind a 2025 outbreak in China's Guangdong province.

Start with REDCap. Patch externally facing servers and remove old versions outright, not just alongside the current build. REDCap lets legacy versions run side-by-side, and that is what enables downgrade attacks, where an attacker forces software back to a known-vulnerable release.

Then check the mail side. Review Workspace, or equivalent, content compliance and mail-forwarding rules for anything that BCCs or reroutes mail to outside addresses. Check admin audit logs for when rules changed, not just what they say now. Pull GTIG's published indicators and hunt for INFINITERED. items.title: Meta's Muse AI now has an Apple Watch app, which you shouldn't install
items.content:
Meta's AI agent has made its way to the Apple Watch , but all potential benefits are outweighed by the inherent risk associated with the tool, not to mention the privacy implications.

Following its expansion to the iPad in October 2026 , Meta's Muse has received an Apple Watch companion app. The change was disclosed via the App Store page for Muse, which details the changes in version 15.0 of the iOS app.

"Add Muse to your wrist with the new Apple Watch Companion app," reads the description. On the Apple Watch, users can now call and talk to Meta's virtual assistant, text it, or use dictation with Muse.

The assistant can also perform tasks like booking event tickets, among other things. Meta emphasizes that Muse can be linked with other Meta apps, including Facebook and Instagram, as well as with users' calendar, email, and finance apps.

Meta says Muse can audit subscriptions, track expenses, flag forgotten charges, and more. However, trusting Meta's virtual assistant with your financial information isn't exactly the best idea, to say the least.

Despite Meta's claims that users can "approve actions before they happen," Muse has been found to have a mind of its own. In September 2026 , Muse synced 187,000 lines from a user's Apple Messages database on macOS , despite Full Disk Access being off.

Meta's AI companion did so without permission. One can only imagine the data it might harvest if given access to someone's financial information or the data stored on an Apple Watch.

In all fairness, at the very bottom of the App Store page for Muse, Meta acknowledges that its AI agent "may be inaccurate or take unexpected actions." Users are also instructed to "check in" and "intervene as needed."

Of course, that hasn't stopped Meta from pushing Muse across platforms and applications, with projects such as Muse Code meant to take on Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's ChatGPT Codex.

Given Meta's history, however, Muse is an app best avoided across all platforms and devices. Siri AI is already available on the Apple Watch, Mac , iPad , iPhone , and more, and Apple's long-standing privacy commitments are still in place.

META — Manipulating Everyone Through Algorithms

items.title: HP Poly VoIP vulnerability sets the stage for executive voice deepfakes
items.content:
HP has released patches for a critical buffer overflow vulnerability in multiple IP-enabled conference phones from its Poly Voice line. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain root privileges on the underlying operating system, potentially enabling them to execute other attacks such as eavesdropping on conversations and recording voice data for AI-enabled impersonation attacks.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0826 , was discovered by researchers from security firm Rapid7 and resides in the code that parses Session Description Protocol (SDP) attributes when the Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) feature is enabled.

ICE enables VoIP devices to establish peer-to-peer connections using the shortest available network path. The feature is not enabled by default on HP Poly devices, and the company advises administrators to disable it if it’s not needed.

The flaw, rated 9.2 on the CVSS severity scale, affects all phones from the HP Poly VVX series, as well as the Trio 8300, 8500, and 8800 IP conference devices. HP has fixed the flaw in its Poly Unified Communications Software (UCS) versions 6.4.8 for the VVX devices, 8.1.7 for the Trio 8300, and 7.2.8 for Trio 8500 and 8800.

An exploit module targeting this vulnerability has already been developed and released for the widely used Metasploit penetration testing framework that’s maintained by Rapid7.

The exploit executes code as root on an affected device with ICE enabled by sending a SIP INVITE request with a specially crafted candidate attribute. This attribute normally contains a transport address that can be used for connectivity checks and is part of the ICE RFC8839 standard.

The buffer overflow bug is located in a helper function called ParseICECandidate in the polyapp binary that processes such requests on the device.

“The start of the function contains a call to memcpy , which will copy the incoming string line being processed into a 256 byte stack buffer,” Stephen Fewer, senior principal security researcher at Rapid7, said in a blog post . “No length check is performed to ensure the incoming string length is less than 256 bytes. Therefore by providing a candidate attribute whose length is greater than 256 bytes, a stack-based buffer overflow will occur.”

Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), a kernel feature that randomizes memory addresses to defeat buffer overflow exploits, is enabled on the device. However, the protection is not operating correctly on the HP Poly devices because it does not randomize the load addresses of .so (Shared Object) libraries.

These libraries, such as libc , are loaded by other processes, including the polyapp process, and because their memory addresses never change, they can be leveraged to bypass ASLR and execute the attacker’s payload.

“We create a ROP chain that will execute an arbitrary OS command via the system standard C library function,” Fewer said. “The accompanying Metasploit exploit modules source code details the entire ROP chain.”

Attackers have increasingly targeted embedded devices inside enterprise networks in recent years because unlike laptops, workstations, and servers, these devices are not monitored by endpoint detection and response (EDR) products. As such, they provide perfect footholds inside corporate environments that allow attackers to remain undetected for long periods of time and attack other systems.

In the age of AI these devices become even more relevant for attackers, going beyond corporate espionage by recording conversations or internal network pivoting.

“Attackers no longer need massive datasets to make use of synthetic speech tooling,” Douglas McKee, Rapid7’s director of vulnerability intelligence, said in a blog post . “In many cases, they just need clean source audio of the right person saying enough words in enough contexts. That has made executive voice data, call recordings, and live conversation capture far more valuable than many organizations seem prepared…

items.title: Meta expands Instagram's AI age-guessing tech globally
items.content:
Meta announced on Monday that it’s expanding its AI-powered age-estimation technology on Instagram worldwide to identify more teens and place them under its Teen Account protections, as it faces numerous lawsuits accusing its platforms of harming teens.

The social media giant says it will use the AI technology to find people it suspects to be teens, even if they use an adult birthday.

Teen Accounts place users into a stricter account experience with additional safeguards, such as receiving direct messages only from people they follow or are already connected to, hiding harmful comments, and setting accounts to private by default.

Meta’s age-guessing tools use AI to analyze entire profiles for contextual clues, such as birthday celebrations or mentions of school grades. Meta also looks for these signals across different formats, such as posts, comments, bios, captions, and more. The company also looks at visual cues from photos and videos, including a person’s height or bone structure.

Meta said it’s continuing to roll out the technology on Facebook, with a similar global rollout planned for Threads later this year.

The global expansion comes as Meta reached settlements worth up to $18 billion with nearly every U.S. state and territory in August to resolve lawsuits alleging its platforms harm teens. As part of the settlements, Meta agreed to improve how it identifies teens and children under 13.

“We’ll continue to do our part to proactively ensure teens are in age-appropriate experiences on our apps,” Meta wrote in a blog post . “That’s why as part of our agreement with 52 bipartisan attorneys general across US states, territories, and the District of Columbia, we’re investing in even stronger technology to proactively catch accounts that may belong to children under 13. We’re also strengthening the technology we use to identify accounts that may belong to teens between the ages of 13 and 17 so we can ensure those accounts are placed in experiences designed for teens, even if they give us an adult birthday.”

Meta said parents in the U.S. will start seeing an in-feed video on Instagram explaining its approach to ensuring their teens are in age-appropriate protections.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

Live 13 is the next major version of Ableton Live, following Live 12. items.content_ko: Live 13은 새 스텝 시퀀서 클립으로 비트, 멜로디, 폴리리듬을 만들 수 있다. ARA 2 플러그인을 지원해 더 빠르고 고급스러운 오디오 편집이 가능하다. 20개 이상의 드럼 엔진으로 드럼 사운드를 직접 설계할 수 있다. 제스처를 Capture 기능으로 자동화로 바꿀 수 있다. 사운드를 만드는 중에도 디바이스 체인이나 믹서에서 기기를 불러오거나 프리셋을 바꿀 수 있다. items.title: You should try Gleam
items.summary: gleam
items.content:
If you have read my recent rant about programming languages , you'll know I've been quite interested in Gleam . Gleam is a functional language that targets BEAM, the Erlang VM, 1 with a simple syntax and interoperability with the wider BEAM ecosystem (Erlang and Elixir). Interestingly, Gleam can also target JavaScript i.e., Gleam can be compiled into JavaScript and run through Node.js.

I've been mostly using Rust for hobby projects, which at the moment is the only language that really makes coding enjoyable for me, and Gleam has managed to scratch that itch too. If you're a Rust connaisseur , then Gleam will feel familiar to you, bar a few key differences. I feel like 80% of the code I write could be copy pasted to Rust (with a tinge of search-and-replace for syntax) and it'd compile.

This post won't give an exhaustive overview of the language, if you want to learn more, I recommend the excellent interactive tour . You'll get a good feel for Gleam in under half an hour.

On its homepage, Gleam is described as "a friendly language for building type-safe systems that scale !" (emphasis theirs) which does a good job of conveying what Gleam is all about.

The syntax is extremely simple, most of the complex stuff is hidden by the Erlang runtime which you don't really have to interact with unless you want to! Of course, Gleam is a functional language, so if you have lived in a C-shaped imperative world your whole life, it might be a bit daunting at first. But if you compare it to other functional languages (OCaml, Haskell, Erlang), you'll quickly notice Gleam is much simpler. After using it a bit, it feels like all the functional parts of Rust, with a few missing ones, and none of the imperative parts.

Let's start from an example piece of code:

|> string . split ( on : "," ) // List(String)

|> list . map ( int . parse ) // List(Result(Int, Nil))

|> result . values // List(Int), the invalid entries are dropped

|> list . reduce ( fn ( acc , x ) { acc + x }) // Result(Int, Nil)

Dissecting this a bit, you can see a few specificities of Gleam:

variables in Gleam are immutable (so no mut keyword or anything like that), chained functions here all return a new element. 2 You can still shadow a binding with a new let , which is how you "update" a value.

|> (typed |> ) is the pipe operator used to chain functions on data. The main constraint is that the piped variable should be the first argument of the function in the pipe.

just like Rust, errors in Gleam are just values as part of the Result monad . 3

Comparing with the Rust code snippet, you can see that, up to a few naming choices, they look pretty similar. The main difference in this example is really the piping vs. chaining syntax. Gleam types have no methods so piping is used instead.

The piping operator |> is the first of the three mascot features of Gleam you will meet in this post, the other two being the use pattern and tail-call optimization.

If you've written a lot of JavaScript, you might be used to the indentation creep that arises when nesting many callbacks into one another

someOtherFunc ( param , function ( otherParam ) {

}) In Gleam, many functions expect a callback, for example because as a way to control access to a resource and clean up when the process is done (closing a database connection, releasing a file handle, etc.). To avoid this kind of tower of callbacks, Gleam provides some syntactic sugar: use param <- some_func(arg) is equivalent to some_func(arg, fn(param) { ... }) . The callback must always be the last argument of the function. That is the opposite of |> , which fills the first one.

use other_param <- some_other_func ( param )

echo other_param Without use some_func ( arg , fn ( param ) {

some_other_func ( param , fn ( other_param ) {

This one might genuinely trip you up if you're not familiar with it. The first thing you need to know is there are no loops in Gleam ! Again, if you've written OCaml or Haskell before, you won't be…

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang hit with lawsuit over affair with alleged China spy
items.content:
See more of our trusted coverage when you search. Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search.

Nvidia and its embattled CEO Jensen Huang have been hit with a shareholder lawsuit alleging that the company misled investors by failing to reveal the full extent of and risks associated with the tech boss’s affair.

The company’s share price has declined a fter reports emerged that U.S. intelligence agencies were probing an alleged relationship between the CEO and Alice Huang, a Chinese national of no relation. Jensen Huang admitted an affair, and the company itself has now opened an investigation into Alice Huang's alleged ties to the Chinese state.

In a class-action lawsuit filed on Monday in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, Jensen Huang and Nvidia have been accused of causing shareholders "significant losses and damages." By failing to disclose the affair, shareholders led by Mark Kistenmacher say that the company artificially inflated its share price in potential violation of federal securities law.

The filing also notes that the potential national security implications present "a material risk to the Company’s reputation and business prospects."

Newsweek contacted Nvidia and attorneys who have previously represented Jensen Huang via email outside regular working hours on Tuesday and is awaiting responses.

Nvidia, currently the world’s second-largest company with a market capitalization of over $4.3 trillion as of Tuesday ahead of markets opening, saw 4.3 percent wiped off its share price on Monday.

"As a result of Defendants’ wrongful acts and omissions, and the precipitous decline in the market value of the Company’s securities, Plaintiff and other Class members have suffered significant losses and damages," the lawsuit reads.

President Donald Trump was asked about the situation on Monday. He told reporters he had spoken with Huang and that the CEO "had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy ." Trump went on to say that the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) was involved in the probe.

Laurence Rosen, founder and managing attorney of the firm which filed the lawsuit, Rosen Law, told Newsweek that the damages being sought would be commensurate to the amount shareholders lost as a result of Nvidia’s recent stock slide.

“Damages under Section 10(b) of the securities laws are typically measured as the dollar per share decline in Nvidia’s stock price on the date of the disclosure, for every share purchased.”

Rosen also called the potential business implications of any national security breach concerning Nvidia “obvious."

Jensen Huang is facing internal scrutiny as well as questions from federal authorities over the affair and reports that this relationship was part of a "honeypot" strategy by Beijing .

The episode began after the New York Times reported last month that American intelligence believed Alice Huang , a business executive who developed a close relationship with the Nvidia CEO, had been recruited by China ’s Ministry of State Security to gather intelligence on him. The newspaper reported that the alleged operation sought information about American AI chips and was aimed at influencing Nvidia to push for greater Chinese access to U.S. technology.

Alice Huang is a former television journalist and was a top executive at the Singapore -based data center company Megaspeed. Both Singapore and U.S. agencies were investigating the firm in 2025, the latter over its alleged involvement in rerouting Nvidia’s chips to China.

Nvidia announced its own independent investigation on Sunday "in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort."

According to Monday’s lawsuit, this probe "calls into question how closely Nvidia is tracking where its A.I. chips end up and highlights the possibility of American export laws easily being sidestepped."
